oilRate.description: A nullable primitive becomes a plain *float64. The alias form `type X *float64` is a named POINTER type, which Go rejects as a method receiver, so the name could never carry UnmarshalJSON or validation.

observedAt.description: Already a plain *time.Time before this change, via the temporal special case added upstream in #570 / #607.

tags.description: Arrays keep their named type: `type X []string` is not a pointer type and can take methods, so the name is not dead weight.

meta.description: Objects keep their named struct and are wrapped in a pointer, which is unchanged.

score.description: A nullable primitive carrying a constraint. Before this change the alias path emitted no UnmarshalJSON at all, so `minimum` was silently dropped and never enforced.

name.description: Same for string constraints: `minLength` was silently dropped.
